hook: Training is the part you can monitor with loss curves. Evaluation is the part you have to design. This lesson builds a unified eval pipeline that takes any trained language model, runs four heterogeneous evals on it, aggregates the results into a per-task report, and ships a local mock LLM-as-judge so the loop runs without a network. The four evals cover the dimensions every shipping model needs: language modelling (perplexity), short-form correctness (exact-match), open-form similarity (token F1), and qualitative scoring (judge).
